raw_text:
Here’s a focused 1-week deload that keeps the same exercise selection while markedly reducing volume and intensity to facilitate recovery and set up the next block. Assumes the client was training 5 days/week with full-gym access and a compound-focused, hypertrophy-oriented split. Adjust the split order to match what the client has been using; the key is the volume/intensity reduction and not the specific day order.

Deload principles for this week
- Volume: Reduce total working sets to ~30–40% of normal (from ~18 sets/session to ~6–8 sets/session).
- Intensity: Reduce load to ~60–70% of the client’s recent working weights or keep RPE ~5–6. Stop 4–5 reps shy of failure.
- Tempo and form: Emphasize pristine technique and controlled eccentrics (2–3 seconds). No grinders.
- Rest periods: 2–3 minutes on compounds, 60–90 seconds on accessories.
- No AMRAPs, no dropsets, no forced reps. Avoid novelty that might cause soreness.
- Optional: Replace one accessory per session with light mobility or breathing drills.

Weekly structure (example 5-day split)
- Day 1: Upper Push (Chest/Shoulders/Triceps)
- Day 2: Lower (Squat emphasis)
- Day 3: Upper Pull (Back/Biceps)
- Day 4: Lower (Hinge emphasis)
- Day 5: Full Upper (Balance/Prehab focus)

Guidance on loads
- Use the same exercises as the client’s main program.
- For each listed exercise: 2–3 sets of 5–8 reps on compounds, 2 sets of 8–12 on accessories at RPE 5–6 (about 60–70% of last week’s top sets). If unsure, start lighter and keep them moving crisply.

Day 1 — Upper Push
- Barbell bench press: 3 sets x 5–6 reps @ RPE 5–6
- Incline DB press: 2 x 8 @ RPE 5–6
- Seated DB shoulder press: 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 5–6
- Cable lateral raise: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 5
- Triceps pressdown: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 5

Day 2 — Lower (Squat emphasis)
- Back squat: 3 x 5 @ RPE 5–6
- Front squat or leg press (whichever is in the client’s plan): 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 5–6
- Romanian deadlift: 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 5–6
- Leg curl: 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 5
- Standing calf raise: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 5

Day 3 — Upper Pull
- Weighted or bodyweight pull-up: 3 x 5–6 @ RPE 5–6
- One-arm DB row or chest-supported row: 2 x 8 @ RPE 5–6
- Lat pulldown (different grip than row): 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 5
- Rear delt fly (cables or machine): 2 x 12 @ RPE 5
- EZ bar curl or DB curl: 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 5

Day 4 — Lower (Hinge emphasis)
- Deadlift (conventional or sumo per program): 3 x 3–5 @ RPE 5–6
- Barbell or DB split squat: 2 x 6–8/leg @ RPE 5–6
- Hip thrust or glute bridge: 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 5–6
- Leg extension: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 5
- Seated calf raise: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 5

Day 5 — Full Upper (technique and balance)
- Overhead press (barbell or DB): 3 x 5 @ RPE 5–6
- Close-grip bench or dips (match usual choice): 2 x 6–8 @ RPE 5–6
- Machine or cable row (stable): 2 x 8–10 @ RPE 5–6
- Cable fly or pec deck: 2 x 10–12 @ RPE 5
- Face pull or band external rotation: 2 x 12–15 @ RPE 4–5

Warm-up and movement prep (each session, 10–12 minutes)
- 3–5 minutes easy cardio to raise temperature.
- 1–2 mobility drills for target joints (e.g., T-spine openers on upper days; hip flexor + ankle mobility on lower days).
- 2–3 ramp-up sets for the first compound: start with the empty bar, then 40–60% and 70% of the day’s working load for 3–5 reps each—stop well shy of fatigue.

Conditioning
- Keep it easy: 1–2 optional low-intensity sessions of 15–25 minutes (Zone 2) or 2–3 brisk walks of 20–30 minutes. Avoid intervals or sled pushes this week.

Recovery and lifestyle targets (deload focus)
- Sleep: 7.5–9 hours/night. Maintain consistent bed/wake times.
- Steps: 6–10k/day to promote circulation without adding fatigue.
- Soft tissue: 5–10 minutes of light foam rolling on high-use areas if it feels good; no aggressive work that creates soreness.
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes daily of gentle mobility for thoracic spine, hips, and shoulders.

Nutrition for the deload
- Calories: Reduce slightly if appetite and activity drop—about 5–10% below your recent hypertrophy intake. If a mass phase continues next block and weight is stable, you can also hold calories steady for recovery.
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day.
- Carbs: Prioritize around training but overall can be modestly lower than peak hypertrophy weeks.
- Fats: Keep at 20–30% of total calories.
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day; add electrolytes if training in heat or sweating heavily.

Autoregulation notes
- If a set reaches RPE 7 or bar speed slows noticeably, cut the set and reduce load by 5–10%.
- If joints or tendons feel irritated on a given lift, swap to the closest low-stress variation for this week only (e.g., high-bar squat instead of low-bar, neutral-grip pressing, trap bar deadlift).
- End every session feeling like you could have done more.

Exit criteria and transition
- You should finish the week with no joint flare-ups, normal or improved sleep, and a return of motivation.
- Resume the next block at planned volumes/intensities; consider starting compounds ~2.5–5% below prior top working loads and ramp over the first week to re-establish momentum.

This structure preserves movement patterns but meaningfully reduces stress to allow supercompensation before the next training block.
